ogTitle: Phuket–Krabi 4-Day Itinerary — Two Andaman Sea Towns
ogDesc: Day one in Phuket Old Town, ferry across to Krabi, then the Separated Sea, Railay and Tiger Cave — real times, prices and routes for the whole trip.
intro: Phuket and Krabi sit on the same Andaman coast, but they feel completely different. Phuket is a town with a Sino-Portuguese old quarter, Hokkien local food and long beaches, while Krabi is all limestone cliffs over the sea, longtail boats and little islands scattered everywhere. This plan rolls both into one trip over 4 days and 3 nights, using a ferry across from Phuket's Rassada Pier to Krabi so you skip the long drive around. We've mapped the times, prices and routes from how it actually runs in 2026, so you can adjust to your own travel dates.

blocks.html: A lot of people assume Phuket and Krabi have to be two separate trips. In reality the two provinces connect really smoothly — about 160 km by road, roughly 2.5–3 hours in a car. But if you want more fun and a bit of sea on the way, take the ferry across the bay instead: it takes about the same time but you get island views the whole route. This plan starts in Phuket first, since flying into Phuket airport is more convenient, then wraps up in Krabi so you can fly home from Krabi airport without doubling back.

blocks.text: Trip overview: 4 days and how to get around

blocks.html: The rough shape is: day one in Phuket town (old quarter + Promthep Cape), day two a morning ferry across to Krabi and into Ao Nang, day three out to the Separated Sea and Railay, and day four a stop at Tiger Cave or Emerald Pool before flying out. If you only have 3 days, just drop day four.

items: Fly in: Phuket airport (HKT) — several direct flights a day from Bangkok
Cross province: ferry from Rassada Pier (Phuket) → Klong Jilad Pier (Krabi), about 2 hours · fare around 900 THB/person · morning departures from 08:30 through midday
Fly out: Krabi airport (KBV) — flights back to Bangkok and onward connections, so no driving back to Phuket
By road instead: if you'd rather not take the boat, a minivan or rental car runs Phuket–Krabi in 2.5–3 hours via Phang Nga

blocks.title: Book ferry tickets ahead
blocks.html: There are only a handful of cross-province ferry runs a day, and in high season (Nov–Apr) they fill up fast. Book online ahead or buy at the pier early in the morning. During the monsoon (May–Oct) the seas can get rough on some days and a run may be cancelled, so check the weather before your travel day.

blocks.text: Day 1 — Phuket Old Town + Promthep Cape

blocks.html: No need to rush to the beach on day one — take in Phuket town first. You can walk the whole old quarter in half a day. The Sino-Portuguese shophouses on Thalang Road have all turned into cafes, galleries and restaurants now, so wander around shooting the street art, then close out the day with sunset at Promthep Cape.

items.activity: Check in to a hotel near Phuket town or Patong, drop your bags, then head out to walk the old quarter
items.note: Staying in the old town makes eating and sightseeing on foot much easier

items.activity: Hokkien noodles at Mee Ton Poe, an old-school shop running since 1946 — stir-fried noodles with pork, fish balls, shrimp and egg
items.note: It's a popular spot and gets busy; go before noon for a shorter queue

items.activity: Walk Thalang Road and Soi Romanee, shoot the old buildings, pop into a cafe to rest and dodge the afternoon heat
items.note: If it lands on a Sunday night, Thalang Road has the big Lard Yai walking street

items.activity: Drive out to Promthep Cape, the southernmost point of the island, and wait for sunset over the Andaman Sea
items.note: Get there 30–40 minutes before sunset for a good spot to stand

items.activity: Dinner of southern Thai food at Tu Kab Khao or One Chun, both set in old shophouses in the town centre
items.note: Tu Kab Khao has a Bib Gourmand and gets busy in the evening, so book a table

blocks.title: The Big Buddha has reopened
blocks.html: The Big Buddha on Nakkerd Hill is open again for visitors to pay respects and take in the view, since 3 March 2026, after closing for repairs following the 2024 landslide. It's open daily 09:00–18:00, so if you have a free morning on day one you can squeeze in a trip up — the view over Chalong and Kata bays is gorgeous.

blocks.text: Day 2 — Ferry across to Krabi and into Ao Nang

blocks.html: Today is the crossing day. Sort your bags out in the morning and head to Rassada Pier — most ferries to Krabi leave from morning through midday and take about 2 hours to reach Klong Jilad Pier in Krabi. From the pier it's another 20–30 minutes by road into Ao Nang, which makes a good base for catching boats out to the islands the next day.

blocks.label: Day 2
blocks.title: Cross the Andaman, settle into Ao Nang

items.activity: Head to Rassada Pier, check your ticket, load your bags
items.note: Rassada Pier is on the east side of Phuket town, so leave room for traffic

items.activity: Ferry leaves Rassada Pier for Krabi, passing island views along the way
items.note: Some runs stop at Phi Phi before continuing — check which line your ticket is for

items.activity: Arrive at Klong Jilad Pier in Krabi, then take a taxi or minivan into Ao Nang
items.note: The ride into Ao Nang runs about 150–300 THB per trip depending on how you negotiate

items.activity: Check in to your Ao Nang hotel, stroll along Nopparat Thara Beach and save your energy
items.note: Late afternoon along the beach is breezy and pleasant

items.activity: Dinner at the Ao Nang Landmark Night Market — grilled seafood, southern dishes, friendly prices
items.note: The market is across from the sea near Nopparat Thara Beach, with plenty to eat

blocks.text: Day 3 — Four Islands, Separated Sea + Railay

blocks.html: Krabi's headline day. The Four Islands tour takes a longtail boat from Ao Nang around Koh Poda, Chicken Island, Koh Tup and Phra Nang Cave at Railay. At low tide a sandbar links the islands together — what's known as the Separated Sea. A half-day longtail tour starts around 895 THB/person, while a full-day speedboat runs a bit more, including snorkeling gear and a boxed lunch.

blocks.label: Day 3
blocks.title: Four Islands, Separated Sea, Railay Beach

items.activity: Longtail or speedboat leaves Ao Nang Beach for Koh Poda and Chicken Island, snorkeling over the coral
items.note: The tour picks you up at your hotel if you booked the package with transfers

items.activity: Reach the Separated Sea (Chicken Island–Koh Tup–Koh Mor), walk the sandbar at low tide and take photos
items.note: The Separated Sea only appears at low tide — check the tide schedule with the tour before booking

items.activity: Stop at Phra Nang Cave and West Railay Beach, eat your boxed lunch, swim off the white sand
items.note: Railay is reachable by boat only; its limestone cliffs are a mecca for rock climbers

items.activity: Keep swimming or watch the climbers at East Railay before the boat takes you back to Ao Nang
items.note: If you want to try climbing there are half-day beginner courses with instructors and full gear

items.activity: Back in Ao Nang, shower and rest, then find seafood for dinner by the beach
items.note: After a full day in the sun, drink plenty of water and reapply sunscreen

blocks.title: Longtail boat or speedboat
blocks.html: Longtails are cheaper and have more local character, but they're slow and rock with the waves. Speedboats are fast and dry and can hit several spots in a day, but cost more. For an easy half-day around the nearby islands, a longtail is plenty. If you want to go further out to Hong Island, a full-day speedboat is the better use of your time.

blocks.text: Day 4 — Tiger Cave / Emerald Pool before flying out

blocks.html: On the last day you swap the sea for some land sightseeing before flying out of Krabi airport. There are two routes to pick from depending on your energy and flight time. The temple-and-view option is Wat Tham Suea (Tiger Cave Temple) — about 1,260 steps up to a view over Krabi from the hilltop, no entry fee but genuinely tiring. The nature option is the Emerald Pool and the Khlong Thom hot springs, clear emerald-green water in the middle of the forest.

items.activity: Pick one route — Tiger Cave Temple's 1,260-step climb to a 360-degree view, or the Emerald Pool plus the Khlong Thom hot springs
items.note: Tiger Cave Temple has no entry fee · the Emerald Pool charges around 400 THB park entry (foreigners), with the hot spring adding about 200 THB

items.activity: Head back into Krabi town, have lunch and pick up some souvenirs
items.note: Krabi town's market has southern food and local goods to choose from

items.activity: Travel to Krabi airport (KBV) and check in for your flight home
items.note: Allow at least 2 hours to reach the airport before your flight

blocks.html: These numbers assume an easygoing trip, nothing too fancy — the core costs you can't really avoid. What you spend on accommodation depends on the level of hotel you pick.

items: Half-day longtail Four Islands tour: from around 895 THB/person (a full-day speedboat costs more)
Emerald Pool: around 400 THB foreigner park entry + about 200 THB for the hot spring (Tiger Cave Temple has no entry fee)
Food: street and market meals 60–150 THB · southern or seafood restaurants 250–500 THB a meal
Town transport / pier transfers: budget 150–300 THB per trip

blocks.html: The Andaman side has clear wet and dry seasons. The clear-water, best-sea window is Nov–Apr, when every ferry runs and the island tours are fully open. From May to Oct it's monsoon — frequent rain, rough waves, and on some days the cross-province ferries and island tours get cancelled. If you have to go in the rainy season, keep a backup land plan (old town, temples, Emerald Pool) and check the forecast every morning.

faq.q: Phuket to Krabi — is the boat or the road better?
faq.a: If you want the sea atmosphere and no traffic, take the ferry from Rassada Pier to Klong Jilad Pier — about 2 hours, fare around 900 THB/person, with runs from morning through midday. If you're traveling in a big group with lots of luggage, or going outside the ferry schedule, a minivan or rental car (2.5–3 hours via Phang Nga) is convenient and more flexible.

faq.q: How many days is right for a Phuket–Krabi trip?
faq.a: 4 days and 3 nights is about right. Day one for Phuket town, day two crossing to Krabi, day three out to the Separated Sea and Railay, day four for Tiger Cave or the Emerald Pool before flying home. If you only have 3 days, drop the last day — it'll just be a bit rushed.

faq.q: Can you see Krabi's Separated Sea every day?
faq.a: Only at low tide, when the sandbar between Chicken Island, Koh Tup and Koh Mor surfaces. The tide schedule changes daily, so before booking a tour, ask the operator when low tide falls that day so they take you at the right time.

faq.q: Can I fly out of Krabi airport without going back to Phuket?
faq.a: Yes. Krabi airport (KBV) has flights back to Bangkok and several onward routes. Plan an open-jaw trip — fly into Phuket, out of Krabi — and you won't waste time backtracking.

faq.q: When is the sea at its best?
faq.a: November to April is the dry season on the Andaman side — clear water, fewer waves, all ferries and island tours running. May to October is monsoon, with frequent rain and some days when boats are cancelled. If you go in the rainy season, have a backup land plan.
